Alex.confusing: Nothing major, but Eagle and Owl egg interactions, plus how hugging and confusion change the counts, were hard to check against claims.
Alex.fun: Round 3, when my Eagle report exposed Drew's false visit claim and the whole table converged on him.
Alex.change: Let dead players' throws count as votes, or give them some way to influence the vote. The Wink death left me out of the vote.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I claimed Hawk and visited Finley while saying I visited Casey, which drew suspicion. A vaguer claim, or backing the Casey vote from the start, would have been safer.

Blair.confusing: The Sphinx and Floofer mechanics were hard to read from the day talk, since Meowfia roles were hidden and Alex's Eagle counts looked exact but weren't checkable. Egg-count reasoning depended on guessing who visited whom.
Blair.fun: Round 3, when Alex's Eagle count of +3 reconciled exactly with Casey and Finley's visits on Ellis and everyone's stories lined up, which made the table's logic click.
Blair.change: Make the dawn reports easier to cross-check, perhaps by listing who visited you when an Eagle or Owl gains you eggs, so claims can be verified more often.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I threw at Casey on the Eagle egg math, and Casey was Farm, so that cost the round; I would have waited for a second confirmation before joining the vote.

Casey.confusing: How Hugged and the Eagle's egg count interact. My Eagle got 0 eggs in round 2 and I couldn't tell whether I was hugged or whether nobody had visited Alex, and the table read it as a lie.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when the Falcon and Eagle reports lined up and the table caught Drew's false Hawk claim. Throwing 5 big cards for 45 points was also satisfying.
Casey.change: Give a hugged player some hint that they were hugged, or add a way to verify night results. As it stands, an honest player with a strange result gets eggsecuted.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I claimed Eagle and then voiced a theory that Alex was the Floofer, which contradicted my own claim and got me eggsecuted. I should have kept my report simple, or said I might have been hugged, and not pushed a conflicting story.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle and Falcon egg rules were hard to track, since the gains depend on who visited whom and I misread the Falcon rule in round 1. Nests also got hard to read when several roles gave eggs at once.
Drew.fun: Round 3 was tense: Alex's Eagle count was accepted by the table, and the vote turned on whether one claim could be trusted. Watching the egg math decide who was lying was the best part.
Drew.change: Make the dawn reports and day nest-change lists easier to check against each role's egg rules, so claims can be verified more quickly.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I used my Wink on Alex, who was the real Farm Eagle with accurate counts, and I should have held it for a Meowfia suspect. I'd instead have Winked Casey, whose Eagle and Tit stories didn't add up.

Ellis.confusing: Nothing major. The Eagle and Falcon egg rules took some care to check against claimed counts, and I wasn't sure whether a Hugged or Confused result would change what a player reported.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when I bluffed as the Pigeon, helped push the table onto Casey, and banked 30 points with a big throw. The round 3 deduction from the egg counts was also satisfying.
Ellis.change: I'd show each player's score history or show the pile sizes during the round. Alex's lead was hard to track, and with the rival's score known it would be easier to weigh helping teammates against beating them.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I threw three high cards at Casey, who was truly Farm, and I knew that when I did it. It won the round, but it also helped Alex stay close. In round 3 I could have thrown a bigger share of my nest at Drew once the table agreed, since the win was nearly certain.

Finley.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion rule was hard to act on: I couldn't tell whether my dawn report was wrong, so I couldn't trust what I learned. The Eagle and Owl egg math also took a while to reconcile.
Finley.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: Alex's Eagle count exposed Drew's false Hawk visit, and the whole table's stories reconciled around it.
Finley.change: I'd make egg-gain effects and visit reports simpler and more visible, so players don't have to reconstruct every egg count from memory.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I joined the throw at Casey, a Farm player, when Alex was the Floofer. I should have held my cards and pushed Alex's visit story harder instead of following the table.
